summary: Created one Anduril defence product-company and future-IPO idea. Enterprise procurement and production awards validate parts of the model, but Anduril remains private without public audited economics, governance, or an IPO filing. Enqueued one bounded Palantir proxy review; no direct exposure, relationship, or strategy was asserted.

evidence.claim: The Army consolidated more than 120 separate Anduril procurement actions into one enterprise contract for commercially available technologies.

evidence.source: US Department of Defense FY2026 weapons book
evidence.claim: Anduril and General Atomics are named Collaborative Combat Aircraft primes in a program with USD 804.4 million of FY2026 funding.
A 2026 framework targets at least 3,000 systems over three years and at least 1,000 annual deliveries, supported by private and public production-capacity investment.
Anduril raised USD 1.5 billion at a USD 14 billion valuation in 2024 to fund the planned Arsenal-1 manufacturing platform.

evidence.source: Palantir Warp Speed and TITAN materials
evidence.claim: Palantir identifies Anduril as a manufacturing customer and TITAN ecosystem partner, but does not quantify Anduril-related revenue.

daily_report_items: Researched Anduril's product-company model: procurement validation is material, but private financials, production conversion, governance, and IPO valuation block direct action; queued Palantir proxy research.
